rationale: Tests understanding of the selective clearing principle (chitin resists KOH while keratin is digested) that underpins the diagnostic utility of the KOH mount.
Tests the critical sampling site knowledge (active margin, not centre) that determines whether the KOH mount yields a true-positive result.
Tests visual recognition of the three major pathogen groups on KOH mount and their correlation with clinical disease patterns — an inherently visual learning point.
Tests the clinical reasoning required when a negative KOH mount conflicts with a convincing clinical picture — a common real-world scenario that demands a corrective second attempt.
Tests recall of site-specific tinea nomenclature, which guides both clinical communication and site-appropriate treatment decisions.
Tests understanding of the molecular basis of terbinafine resistance (SQLE mutations) driving India's chronic dermatophytosis epidemic.
Tests ability to identify the correct investigation for distinguishing tinea from its common clinical mimics — the central learning point of the differential diagnosis block.
Tests the key management decision of switching to itraconazole when KOH-confirmed tinea fails terbinafine — a common and high-stakes clinical scenario in Indian practice.
Tests understanding that tinea capitis mandates systemic therapy because topical agents cannot penetrate the infected hair shaft — a high-yield management principle.
